skill.name: Sentence openers that put the message up front
skill.why: Readers notice the start of a sentence most. Put what matters there.
skill.how: Ask what the reader needs first. Put that at the start of the sentence.

beats.say: Readers notice the start of a sentence the most.
So put the big message first.
beats.show: **The chairlift is broken.** Take the ladders instead.

beats.say: Hide it at the end, and readers might miss it.
beats.show: Because of the wild wind last night, **the chairlift is broken**.

beats.say: In a story, the start can tell readers when or where.
beats.show: **At midnight,** the snowman blinked. **Behind the hut,** something giggled.

beats.say: That first chunk is called the opener. Make it count.

encounters.frame: Zed is writing a walkthrough for the Ice Palace level. The Frontnip is stuck in the Kitchen.
encounters.text: The Ice Palace is the hardest level in Frostbite Quest, and Zed has finally written a walkthrough for it. The palace has four rooms, which players must clear in this order: the Great Hall, the Kitchen, the Library and the Throne Room. Zed starts each sentence by naming the room, so a player who is stuck can find their place in the walkthrough at a glance. In the Great Hall, a swarm of ice bats swoops from the ceiling, so keep moving and never stand still under the chandelier. In the Kitchen, the frozen chef throws icicles shaped like fish fingers, which you can dodge by ducking behind the giant fridge. In the Library, every book is a trap, apart from the blue one on the bottom shelf, which opens a secret door. ___, the Ice Queen waits on a throne of frozen custard, and she can only be defeated by a well-aimed snowball to the crown. Zed says the custard throne is the most disgusting thing he has ever seen in a game, and he has played Sewer Slugs 3.
